questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
Controls how fast air leaves the storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air entering the storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air leaving the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: Always drive so your vehicle can stop:

options.text: Within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within the distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Always drive so you can stop completely within the area of road you can see ahead of you.

questions.question: Multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions are used to:

options.text: Make a vehicle run more smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide extra gears.
questions.explanation: Multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions provide extra gears. They are controlled by a selector knob on the gearshift lever.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park the vehicle:
questions.correctAnswerText: Within 300 feet of a bridge.
questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Park only briefly and at least 5 feet from the road.

questions.question: Which is NOT a tire problem to check for?

options.text: Recapped tires on the front of a school bus.
All tires made by the same company.

questions.correctAnswerText: All tires made by the same company.
questions.explanation: Check tires for low or high air pressure, excessive wear, cuts or damage, tread separation, dual tires touching each other, mismatched sizes, mixing radial and bias-ply tires, cracked valve stems, and regrooved or recapped tires on school bus front wheels. The manufacturer does not matter.

questions.question: A vehicle should have all of the following, EXCEPT:

options.text: Warning devices for parked vehicles, like flares.

questions.correctAnswerText: A spotlight.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have a fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless equipped with circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles like triangles, fuses, or flares. A spotlight is not required.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?
questions.correctAnswerText: Between three-quarters and one second.
questions.explanation: The average driver's reaction time is between three-quarters and one second.

questions.question: A one-way check valve:

options.text: Drains water and compressor oil from the air tanks.
Prevents air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
Activates the emergency brakes when there is a leak.
Holds the spring brakes in place until used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve sits between the air compressor and the first main reservoir. It prevents air from escaping the system if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?
questions.correctAnswerText: An eight-sided red knob.
questions.explanation: On newer vehicles, the trailer air supply control is an eight-sided red knob. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift.
questions.explanation: Always downshift before entering a curve. Slowing down before the curve lets you control the vehicle better throughout the turn.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Brake harder than in a vehicle without ABS.
Use extra braking force to make the ABS work.
Brake the same way as in a vehicle without ABS.
Brake with less force than in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way as in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way in a vehicle with ABS as you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: With low beam headlights on, how far ahead can you see?
questions.correctAnswerText: 250 feet
questions.explanation: Low beam headlights let you see about 250 feet ahead. At night, drive slowly enough to stop within the distance your headlights show.

questions.question: In an emergency, when using controlled braking, you should:

options.text: Brake as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Brake with about half your normal force.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Keep the steering wheel steady while braking this way.

questions.question: Why should you check tires often in very hot weather?

options.text: Air pressure may increase with the heat.
The lug nuts may come loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase with the heat.
questions.explanation: Heat makes air expand. Tire air pressure can reach dangerously high levels in very hot weather. If this happens, stop and let the tires cool. Do not release air, as the pressure will drop too low once the tires cool down.

questions.question: When you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving and finish the trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and take a nap.
questions.explanation: The only way to safely handle drowsiness is to stop and sleep. Caffeine and other drugs may help briefly, but you will become more tired when they wear off.

questions.question: If your vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives crashes, what should you do?

options.text: Do not warn others about the danger.
Keep the explosives in the vehicle until after moving the vehicles apart.
Remove the explosives from the vehicle before moving the vehicles apart.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the explosives from the vehicle before moving the vehicles apart.
questions.explanation: If you crash while carrying Class 1 explosives, warn others, keep people away, and do not allow smoking near the vehicle. Before separating the vehicles, remove all explosives and place them at least 200 feet away from the vehicles and any buildings.

questions.question: What can you do to avoid driving aggressively?

options.text: Plan trips without extra time for traffic.
Drive slowly in the left lane.
Do not make gestures at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make gestures at other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, plan trips realistically and allow extra time for traffic. Do not tailgate. Do not drive slowly in the left lane or gesture at other drivers.

questions.question: What is true about Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?

options.text: They work with other brake systems and do not reduce braking power.
They do not work well on larger vehicles.
They are illegal in some states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They work with other brake systems and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works alongside your normal brakes. It does not increase or decrease braking power. ABS activates when you brake hard to prevent the wheels from locking.

questions.question: There may be restrictions on transporting explosives or hazardous materials in some areas. What should you do?

options.text: These restrictions are usually not important.
These restrictions do not apply on weekends.
Research these restrictions before choosing your route.
These restrictions only apply if carrying over 1,000 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Research these restrictions before choosing your route.
questions.explanation: Before transporting hazardous materials, look up any restrictions that apply to the routes you plan to take.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
The temperature of air in the brake system.
The pressure of air from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is going to the brakes. Not all air brake vehicles have this gauge.
